title: Redwood cost economics discovery with Dalton Capital
topics: hosted vs dedicated vs private economics
summary: Discovery focused on unit economics for text generation at scale. Dalton Capital is evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment; primary concerns are predictable cost per 1M tokens, batching/caching levers, and integration with their VPC/KMS. Agreed next steps: send detailed pricing model, run a 1-week pilot benchmark, and share security/SOC2 docs.
next_steps: Alice to send detailed pricing spreadsheet and sample cost model by 2026-03-06
Ben to schedule pilot benchmark run with Dalton's sample workload week of 2026-03-16
Share SOC2/ISO docs and network architecture checklist by 2026-03-05
Follow-up call to review pilot results and finalize Dedicated sizing week of 2026-03-23

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Time: 16:00 PST
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Alice Moreno (Redwood AE), Ben Kwan (Redwood SE), Ethan Park (Head of ML Ops - Dalton), Maya Singh (CTO - Dalton), Liam O'Connor (Finance), Jordan Blake (Platform Eng)

Summary: quick discovery to understand cost/unit economics, where they sit with budgets, and technical constraints (VPC, KMS).

[00:00] Alice: Hey everyone thanks for joining, I'm Alice with Redwood, this is Ben on our sys team, how's it going?
[00:08] Ethan: Hey Alice, thanks, doing good, we wanted to get through our cost questions, budget numbers, and what a pilot would look like.
[00:14] Ben: cool, want to kick off with a quick overview of how we price and the levers you can pull for cost per token?
[00:21] Maya: yes please, and also differences between Hosted, Dedicated and Private from a unit-econ standpoint.
[00:28] Ben: sure, so high level Hosted is usage-based per-token with tiered discounts, Dedicated is reserved capacity with a monthly commit so you get a lower per-token compute cost at steady throughput, Private adds ops overhead but gives you full control over network and keys.
[00:44] Liam: when you say per-token, is that input+output tokens or just output? we need to map against our billing model.
[00:50] Alice: typically it's counted as input+output, we show both in the pricing sheet. for economic modeling we usually quote per 1M tokens and also show batch/caching impacts.
[00:59] Ethan: can you give a concrete example? like if we do a 512-token chat and average 200 tokens generated, what's the cost roughly?
[01:07] Ben: ballpark: on Hosted a 512+200 exchange might be X cents per 1k tokens depending on model, but more importantly batching and KV caching can reduce the effective per-token cost. if you can prefix-cache common prompts you'll save a lot.
[01:22] Jordan: when you say KV cache, does that mean keeping the kv states between requests? how does that work across requests from different users?
[01:29] Ben: yes, it's the KV cache for the attention key/value we're careful there - we cache repeated prefixes or system prompts, it's safe because it's per-tenant, and with Dedicated you get longer-lived caches and better hit rates. sometimes the transcript converts KV to K-V cash in the auto notes so ignore that.
[01:45] Maya: security is huge for us - we need VPC peering, customer KMS, SOC2 and logs for audits. what's supported on Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private?
[01:53] Alice: Hosted supports SOC2 and encrypted at rest, but Dedicated gives you VPC peering and customer-managed KMS integrations; Private gives you full air-gapped or on-prem options if required. we'll share the compliance pack.
[02:08] Liam: from finance perspective, we need predictable monthly spend. Dedicated's reserved capacity looks attractive but we need to model utilization. what utilization do you see for customers to make Dedicated worthwhile?
[02:18] Ben: typically 60-70% sustained utilization makes Dedicated cost-effective versus Hosted. if your workload is spiky you can combine reserved with burst capacity. we can model your qps and average token-per-request to give a payback window.
[02:29] Ethan: okay, here's our rough numbers: 2M requests/month, avg 350 tokens in/out, peak qps 45, mostly trading desk assistants and research summarization. Budget for inference is roughly $15k/month initial and can grow to $60k if results are good.
[02:44] Alice: good, that gives us a baseline. we'll plug those into a model but immediate thought: batching at the GPU level can drop per-token cost by 20-40% if latency SLOs allow a small wait, and prefix KV caching for standard prompts could cut costs further for summarization.
[03:00] Jordan: latency SLO is important - many of our use cases are sub-300ms. can batching still help?
[03:06] Ben: yes, continuous batching with small time windows (like 10-30ms) can give gains without harming p95 too much; for low-latency endpoints we recommend hybrid routing: route latency-sensitive calls to low-batch pools and bulk jobs to high-batch pools.
[03:21] Maya: curious about model selection - are you optimizing for quantized models? we use LLMs for sensitive data and want good privacy and cost.
[03:29] Ben: we support quantized variants and select kernels per model/length. quantization reduces memory and compute cost but test for quality. part of our pilot is A/Bing model variants with your prompts to ensure quality vs cost tradeoff.
[03:45] Ethan: do you have tooling to estimate per prompt token count before sending? our engineers want to forecast monthly costs per feature.
[03:52] Alice: yes we provide tokenization helpers in the SDK and a cost-estimator dashboard where you can upload sample logs and we run simulations with batching and cache assumptions. we'll include that in the pricing pack.
[04:04] Liam: can you run a cost scenario: 2M requests, 350 tokens average, no caching vs 30% cache hit rate, Hosted pricing vs Dedicated reserved?
[04:12] Ben: absolutely, that's a perfect pilot input. we can show Hosted nominal to Dedicated ROI at different utilization / cache hit break-even points.
[04:20] Maya: legal asks: we might need a private deployment for regulated desks, what does timeline and cost look like for Private?
[04:27] Alice: Private is higher up-front (setup, support, maybe on-prem hardware) and longer procurement cycles, typically 3-6 months to stand up. the unit cost can be similar to Dedicated after amortizing infra, but there's a platform license. we'll map that out in a detailed quote.
[04:40] Ethan: any gotchas with tokenization - we use a lot of HTML and docs, token counts spike, so accurate estimation matters.
[04:46] Ben: yep, we can ingest your sample payloads to characterize token distribution - average and heavy tail. that also feeds into batching and sequence length tuning which affects kernel selection. sometimes transcripts say K8s or K-b-s wrong, but we'll be explicit in the docs.
[05:02] Jordan: on Dedicated, how does burst capacity billing work? if we get a sudden spike, are we charged a premium?
[05:09] Alice: bursts are charged at a higher rate but capped per policy; you can configure automatic fallback to Hosted if Dedicated pools are saturated. that's one of our resilience features.
[05:18] Liam: for forecasting, we'd rather see a blended per-token estimate with conservative and optimistic scenarios.
[05:24] Alice: we'll provide three scenarios: conservative (low cache, low batching), expected, and aggressive (high cache, good batching). each will include model variant assumptions.
[05:33] Ethan: want to talk pilot specifics - we'll give you a week of logs and 10k test prompts, want you to run benchmarks and return cost per token and latency distribution.
[05:41] Ben: yes, we'll run microbenchmarks on Hosted and Dedicated replica pools, test batching windows and cache TTLs. goal is to produce a recommended config and cost delta.
[05:50] Maya: timeline - legal procurement needs papers by mid-March if we proceed. can you get security docs and a draft SOW soon?
[05:58] Alice: yes, security pack by end of week, draft SOW and pricing by Friday.
[06:05] Liam: competitors - we're also talking to OpenAI and Anthropic about custom contracts; curious how Redwood compares on unit economics.
[06:12] Ben: we typically land between raw cloud infra and large providers: better per-token economics than vanilla cloud API at scale because of batching and Dedicated pricing, and more control than public LLM endpoints. we'll include a comparative slide.
[06:25] Ethan: a few quick technical Qs: does Redwood support customer-managed keys for Hosted?
[06:30] Alice: Hosted supports bring-your-own-key via KMS for enterprise customers in select regions; Dedicated and Private support it fully. we'll confirm region availability in the security pack.
[06:40] Jordan: about telemetry - we need token-level cost breakdowns per route and tracing hooks to debug latency spikes.
[06:46] Ben: that's in Redwood Console: per-route cost/latency, trace ids, and logs. we can add custom metrics via our tracing SDK.
[06:54] Maya: can you support SSO and RBAC integration with our existing IDP?
[06:58] Alice: yes SAML/SSO and role-based access are supported for Dedicated and Private; Hosted supports SSO for enterprise tiers.
[07:06] Liam: ok let's recap next steps.
[07:09] Alice: recap: we'll send pricing spreadsheet and three scenarios, security/compliance pack, run a benchmark with your sample logs, propose Dedicated sizing and burst policy. Ben will own the pilot run. any deadlines?
[07:20] Maya: we'd like the docs by this Friday and a pilot scheduled second week of March.
[07:25] Ethan: I'll upload logs and sample prompts to the secure bucket you share.
[07:28] Alice: perfect, we'll follow up with calendar invite for the pilot kick-off.
[07:32] Liam: thanks everyone, excited to see the numbers.
[07:36] Ben: thanks, talk soon.
[07:39] End of transcript. Note: occasional transcription errors for acronyms and product names, e.g., KV cache sometimes appears as K-V cash, Redwood product names truncated in auto captions.
